name: Shear Bands
desc: A packing of grains under compression, where the load refuses to spread out evenly — it finds a few paths and rides them, so a sparse blazing network of force chains carries almost everything while its neighbours idle, and strain refuses to stay uniform too, localising into inclined seams where grains climb over each other and the packing loosens until it can no longer hold anything, so the chains route around the band and it goes dark: force network, sand under a lamp, false-colour DEM, contact-graph schematic or a CT slice.

energy.doc: applied load and how fiercely the force chains glow — max drives the network white-hot and thick

density.doc: grain count — 0 is a coarse gravel of big discs, 1 a fine sand of hundreds

scale.doc: grain size relative to the frame — max packs in far more, finer grains

speed.doc: loading rate: how fast the sample is squeezed and how quickly bands nucleate and hand over

dilate.doc: dilatancy — how much the shear band loosens as grains climb over each other, and so how hard it unloads and goes dark

hue.doc: mineral hue of the grains (the force network keeps its own hot palette)

style.doc: aesthetic: the classic dark-field force network, grains dim and chains incandescent / real sand under a warm lamp / false-colour discrete-element figure, every grain painted by its load / contact-graph schematic in pure line on paper, no grains at all / X-ray CT slice where the dilated band reads as a low-density seam

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the packing disorder, the load-splitting fractions and the band geometry
